"Rush Rush" is a song by American singer Paula Abdul, taken from her second studio album, Spellbound (1991). It was released on April 24, 1991, by Virgin Records as the lead single from the album. Written by Peter Lord and produced by Peter Lord and V. Jeffrey Smith (both members of the Family Stand), the song achieved success in the United States, where it topped the Billboard Hot 100, and became a worldwide hit.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
"Rush Rush" was a departure for Abdul stylistically, as it was her first [[ballad]] released as a single, following the six uptempo singles from her debut LP. Lyrically, "Rush Rush" is about the desire for a lover who will give their all in a relationship.

First presented to Abdul as a demo by the Family Stand in 1990, she became intent on it becoming ''Spellbound''<nowiki/>'s first single. In late 1990 at Studio Masters, Abdul laid down a [[scratch vocal]] for the track, which was never intended to make it to the song's final mix. However, the producers felt that its unpolished sound was needed to give the song its ingenuous tone, to match its subject matter and accompanying promotional video clip. The scratch vocal ended up on the final cut in March 1991.{{citation needed|date=February 2025}}

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: "Rush Rush" debuted on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] at number 36 on May 11, 1991, and reached number one five weeks later, on June 15, 1991, remaining there for five consecutive weeks. At the time, it was the longest-running number one since [[Madonna (entertainer)|Madonna]]'s "[[Like a Virgin (song)|Like a Virgin]]" spent six weeks at number one during 1984 and 1985. The song also spent five weeks atop the ''Billboard'' [[Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks|Adult Contemporary]] chart. The song was ranked as the 64th-most-successful song of the 1990s in the United States.<ref name="usde"/> On the Billboard All Time chart between 1958 to 2018, the song ranked as the 77th-most successful single of all time in the United States.<ref name="usat"/> Outside of the U.S., the song also reached number one in Canada and number two in Australia. In the United Kingdom, "Rush Rush" peaked at number six on the [[UK Singles Chart]].
sections.text: "Rush Rush" debuted on the US Billboard Hot 100 at number 36 on May 11, 1991, and reached number one five weeks later, on June 15, 1991, remaining there for five consecutive weeks. At the time, it was the longest-running number one since Madonna's "Like a Virgin" spent six weeks at number one during 1984 and 1985. The song also spent five weeks atop the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart. The song was ranked as the 64th-most-successful song of the 1990s in the United States. On the Billboard All Time chart between 1958 to 2018, the song ranked as the 77th-most successful single of all time in the United States. Outside of the U.S., the song also reached number one in Canada and number two in Australia. In the United Kingdom, "Rush Rush" peaked at number six on the UK Singles Chart.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The video reimagines the 1955 [[James Dean]]/[[Natalie Wood]] film ''[[Rebel Without a Cause]]'', including iconic [[Location shooting|location]] shots at [[Griffith Observatory]], a black [[Mercury Eight|1949 Mercury]], and a climactic street race. With [[Keanu Reeves]] filling James Dean's role of Jim, opposite Abdul as Judy, several scenes from the movie are duplicated shot-for-shot. The video was directed by Stefan Würnitzer in April 1991 and produced by Karen Rohrbacher for [[Lucasfilm|Lucasfilm Commercial Productions]]. The British ''[[Top of the Pops]]'' aired an alternate version of the video, re-edited to contain more "performance shots" and less story. Many more shots of Abdul dancing in the orange dress were present.{{citation needed|date=February 2025}}
